intended_object: The eigenspace ker(A − μI) ⊆ 𝕜ⁿ of a Hermitian matrix A for a scalar μ, i.e. the eigenspace of the linear operator x ↦ A x on Euclidean space. Taken from the docstring.
explanation:
`A.lin` is the continuous linear map whose underlying linear map is `A.mat.toEuclideanLin`, i.e. multiplication by A on `EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n`. The definition applies Mathlib's `Module.End.eigenspace` to this map at μ, so it gives exactly {x | A x = μ x}, as the docstring says. Nothing goes wrong in edge cases: when μ is not an eigenvalue the result is ⊥. It also holds for every μ ∈ 𝕜, not only real μ.

The setting (an RCLike field, a finite index type, Hermitian matrices) is the one that `HermitianMat` itself is built on. The definition is a thin wrapper around Mathlib's general `Module.End.eigenspace`, not a re-implementation of it in a special case. So it is not too narrow.
